title: The day the Mississippi River ran backward 🌊
subject: earthquake
description:
Could this happen in the middle of America again? 👇

In the winter of 1811–1812, three magnitude 7+ earthquakes hit the New Madrid area of Missouri and Arkansas. Witnesses saw the Mississippi flow upstream, the river briefly got waterfalls, and the ground sank into what is now Reelfoot Lake.

Sources: USGS ("Summary of 1811-1812 New Madrid Earthquakes Sequence"), Wikipedia ("1811–1812 New Madrid earthquakes", eyewitness account of Eliza Bryan, 1816), UC Santa Barbara Geography

scenes.text: In New Madrid, Missouri, Eliza Bryan saw the current turn "retrograde for a few minutes."
A magnitude 7.5 earthquake had just hit, on December 16, 1811.
Two more struck by February. One lifted the riverbed and made waterfalls at Kentucky Bend.
Chimneys fell as far away as Cincinnati, and the shaking reached nearly 1 million square miles.
In Tennessee, the ground sank up to 20 feet and flooded. It's still there, called Reelfoot Lake.
